B. Fiscal Policy Framework for the FY 2026/27 and the Medium-
Term Budget
27. The fiscal policy for FY 2026/27 and the medium term will be
anchored on a growth-supportive consolidation strategy that advances the
Government’s priorities under Bottom - Up Economic Transformation
Agenda (BETA) and the Fourth Medium Term Plan. The policy will also
integrate the Government’s emerging initiatives in human capital
development, agricultural transformation, energy, and transport and
logistics. This approach is intended to slow the pace of public debt
accumulation, strengthen debt sustainability, and support the
implementation of a proactive liability-management framework, while
safeguarding the quality of public services. Fiscal consolidation efforts will
prioritize enhanced domestic revenue mobilization, rigorous expenditure
optimization and reprioritization, and protection of essential government
programs and social interventions.
28. In line with the fiscal consolidation plan, the overall fiscal deficit is
projected to gradually decline from 5.3 percent of GDP in the FY 2026/27
to 3.6 percent of GDP in the FY 2027/28 and further to 3.3 percent of GDP
in the FY 2028/29. This will strengthen the country’s debt position and
ensure the country’s development agenda is sustainably funded.
29. In the FY 2026/27 budget, total revenues including Appropriation-in-
Aid (A-i-A) are projected at KSh 3,629.7 billion (17.4 percent of GDP) from
KSh 3,399.1 billion (18.2 percent of GDP) in the FY 2025/26 (Table 2).
Of this, ordinary revenue is projected at KSh 2,985.7 billion (14.3 percent
of GDP) from KSh 2,784.4 billion (14.9 percent of GDP) in the FY 2025/26.
30. Over the medium term, as a percent of GDP, the Government’s total
revenue including AiA is projected to increase from 17.4 percent of GDP
in the FY 2026/27 to 17.5 percent of GDP in the FY 2027/28 and moderate
to 16.9 percent of GDP in the FY 2028/29. Of the total revenue, ordinary
revenue is projected to increase from 14.3 percent of GDP in the FY
2026/27 to 14.7 percent of GDP in the FY 2027/28 and moderate to 14.3
percent of GDP in the FY 2028/29.

31. The overall expenditures and net lending are projected at KSh
4,785.2 billion (23.0 percent of GDP) in the FY 2026/27 from KSh 4,638.4
billion (24.9 percent of GDP) in the FY 2025/26. The FY 2026/27
comprises: recurrent expenditure of KSh 3,538.7 billion (17.0 percent of
GDP); development expenditure of KSh 749.0 billion (3.6 percent of GDP);
transfers to County Governments of KSh 495.5 billion and Contingency
Fund of KSh 2.0 billion, respectively.
32. Total expenditure is projected to decrease from 23.0 percent of GDP
in the FY 2026/27 to 21.3 percent of GDP in the FY 2027/28 to 20.4
percent of GDP in the FY 2028/29. Of the total expenditures, recurrent
expenditure is projected to decline from 17.0 percent of GDP in the FY
2026/27 to 15.4 percent of GDP in the FY 2027/28 and further to 14.5
percent of GDP in the FY 2028/29 while development expenditure is
expected to rise from 3.6 percent of GDP in the FY 2026/27 to 3.8 percent
of GDP in the FY 2027/28 and 4.1 percent of GDP in the FY 2028/29.
33. Consistent with the projected expenditures and revenues, the fiscal
deficit including grants is projected at KSh 1,111.8 billion (5.3 percent of
GDP) in the FY 2026/27 budget compared to the projected fiscal deficit of
KSh 1,199.4 billion (6.4 percent of GDP) in the FY 2025/26. The fiscal
deficit in the FY 2026/27 will be financed by a net external financing of
KSh 116.2 billion (0.6 percent of GDP) and a net domestic financing of
KSh 995.7 billion (4.8 percent of GDP).
